meta.intro: Today's throughline: open weights and cheap specialization are racing ahead, while Japan chooses between catching up and owning niches.
meta.briefingTitle: Thinking Machines Teases Near-Frontier Open Weights, AI Starts Proving Theorems, and Japan Bets on Pre-Training and Chip Niches
meta.summary: The common thread is who gets to own and tune capable models. Thinking Machines shipped a 594B MoE with Apache 2.0 weights promised, Sequoia and a16z funded the tuning and agent-desktop layers around such models, and AI-written proofs of old theory conjectures began arriving faster than experts can review them. Meanwhile US-China chip flows jammed, with 600,000 H200s stuck in Hong Kong. Japan's answers are Sakana's first from-scratch pre-training plan and niche hardware like EUV pellicles, against a US lead that is still measured in years.

gaps.label: Sovereign frontier-model pretraining
gaps.note: Up one — Sakana announced Sawara, its first from-scratch pre-training plan, but weights are not due until spring 2027 and no GPU budget is disclosed.

gaps.label: Depth of private risk capital for AI infrastructure
gaps.note: Unchanged — Sequoia, a16z and Elad Gil wrote $45M-$350M rounds in a week, while Japan's visible rounds were pre-seed and ¥850M.

gaps.label: Domestic leading-edge chip manufacturing
gaps.note: Unchanged — PFN-Tenstorrent chiplets are a five-year research plan and AirMembrane's pellicle line is 2028; no new fab capacity.

gaps.label: Early-stage AI venture formation
gaps.note: Up one — ANRI launched a pre-seed program and backed a UTokyo spinout, but round sizes remain a fraction of US seeds like Phaze's $8.75M.

items.headline: Thinking Machines Ships Inkling 2 Small: a 594B MoE With 17B Active Parameters, Apache 2.0 Weights Promised Only After Red-Teaming
items.dek: Murati's lab sells a closed API first and promises open weights next week, an unusual open-weight sequence.

analysis.happening: Released Nov 5 on Tinker: 594B-parameter MoE, 17B active, image input. Vendor-reported 31 on the Artificial Analysis Index and 86.3% on SWE-bench Pro Hard. Tinker pricing reportedly $0.30/$1.00 per million input/output tokens. Weights stay closed until external safety testing ends.
analysis.now: If Apache 2.0 weights land, builders get a near-frontier coding model to fine-tune and self-host, a hedge against closed-lab pricing. Caveat: benchmarks are vendor-reported, other models lead many rows, and one outlet says cost per task rose sharply.
analysis.future: Watch whether weights drop the week of Nov 9-13, which clouds host it, and independent SWE-bench reruns. Fine-tuning-as-a-service on Tinker is the business model to study.

items.headline: AI-Produced Proofs Pile Up: OpenAI and Anthropic Claim to Refute the Exponential Time Hypothesis, and PSI Claims the Aaronson-Ambainis Conjecture
items.dek: Lean-checked machine proofs of decades-old theory problems now arrive within weeks of each other while human review lags.

analysis.happening: OpenAI (Oct 26) and Anthropic separately posted proofs that 3-SAT has a 2^o(n) algorithm, refuting ETH; both passed Lean. On Nov 6, Physical Superintelligence said a system on a non-public Anthropic model proved the 2008 Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture, with Lean verifying.
analysis.now: Lean checks only the statement it is given, and the PSI claim is self-published without peer review. The scarce layer is expert review, so proof-verification tooling and Lean formalization services are the opening.
analysis.future: Watch Ryan Williams' review verdict on ETH and a Stanford write-up of Aaronson-Ambainis. A confirmed refutation would reprice hardness results that rest on ETH.

items.headline: Sequoia Leads a $45M Series A at $300M for Trajectory, an 18-Person Post-Training Startup Already Serving Harvey, Rogo and Decagon
items.dek: Continual learning as a product: lawyers and doctors retrain open models from app feedback without an ML team.

analysis.happening: Trajectory (SF, about a year old, 18 staff) raised $45M led by Sequoia with Nvidia, Bessemer and Bain Capital Ventures at $300M. A self-serve platform collects app feedback and retrains open-source models. Named customers: Harvey, Rogo, Decagon, Mercor, Nvidia.
analysis.now: Sequoia is betting post-training is the next layer to productize, replacing forward-deployed engineers. Caveat: outlets conflict on prior funding and the pre/post-money is unstated. Rivals include Thinking Machines' Tinker and Prime Intellect.
analysis.future: Watch for outcome data against frontier models and more vertical customers. A Japanese-language or regulated-industry variant is a gap an AWS-fluent builder could target.

items.headline: a16z Leads an $8.75M Seed for Phaze, Where Parsec's Founders Give AI Agents Their Own Governed PCs
items.dek: Remote GPU desktops with an MCP server so computer-use agents can run CAD or 3D software where APIs fail.

analysis.happening: Phaze, founded by Benjy Boxer and Chris Dickson (Parsec, sold to Unity in 2021), raised $8.75M led by a16z with Indie, NextView, Makers Fund and NYC's Lerer Hippeau. Agents drive desktops through a local MCP server, with directory sync and audit logs.
analysis.now: The bet: agents need full desktops where APIs do not exist, such as CAD and GPU work. Caveat: the MCP integration is labeled experimental and performance claims are company-reported.
analysis.future: A builder can try the MCP server now. Watch whether desktops-for-agents becomes a category and how AWS WorkSpaces and Nvidia respond.

items.headline: Oracle Drops a $7B Tencent Chip Lease While 600,000 Nvidia H200s Sit Stuck in Hong Kong
items.dek: Washington and Beijing are both closing the remote-compute loophole, leaving China-bound inventory in limbo.

analysis.happening: FT reports Oracle cancelled a five-year, roughly $7B deal giving Tencent access to about 100,000 advanced chips in Southeast Asia. Reuters (Nov 5) says about 600,000 H200s are parked in Hong Kong because Beijing withholds import approval.
analysis.now: China-linked demand is blocked from both ends, so offshore neocloud capacity loses a marquee tenant. Caveat: the Oracle story rests on one FT report with anonymous sources and no company comment.
analysis.future: Watch Nvidia's China line in guidance, Oracle's Southeast Asia utilisation, and whether rules extend to remote access. Domestic Chinese accelerators are the beneficiaries.

items.headline: Sakana AI Moves Into From-Scratch Pre-Training: 'Sawara' Targets Hundreds of Billions of Parameters, Small Model Weights in Spring 2027
items.dek: Japan's best-funded lab stops at post-training open models and plans its own base model.

analysis.happening: At its Oct 26 Tokyo symposium, Sakana named pre-training, post-training (Namazu) and orchestration (Fugu) as its sovereignty pillars. Sawara Small pre-training starts Dec 2026 with weights planned for spring 2027; a larger model targets hundreds of billions of parameters.
analysis.now: Gap: US labs already pre-train at frontier scale, while Sakana's edge is Japanese defense, cyber and finance buyers wanting no US or Chinese API. Caveat: no GPU budget disclosed, the plan is stated intent, and naming is provisional.
analysis.future: Watch for GPU partners, Sawara Small benchmarks against Qwen and Llama at similar size, and whether the Oct 28 enterprise API early access pulls in sovereign customers.

items.headline: Simulacra Takes an ANRI Pre-Seed for a UTokyo-Born Model That Digitally Twins How People Think
items.dek: ANRI's first backing under its new Pre-Seed Program, built on Izumi Lab research.

analysis.happening: Simulacra (founded Sept 2025, University of Tokyo engineering research) raised an undisclosed pre-seed from ANRI. It builds interview AI plus consumer, economic and urban digital twins, and joined a JST AI-for-Science project starting Oct 2026.
analysis.now: US analogs are synthetic-persona and market-simulation startups; Japan's angle is academic social-science agent simulation sold to municipal and policy buyers. Caveat: amount undisclosed, no customers stated, and validity versus real behaviour is unproven.
analysis.future: Watch for seed size, first municipal or enterprise pilots, and whether ANRI's pre-seed program backs more university-spinout AI labs.

items.headline: AirMembrane Raises About ¥850M for Graphene EUV Pellicles, Targeting a 2028 Mass-Production Line
items.dek: A Tsukuba AIST spinout aims at a consumable that Rapidus and TSMC fabs both depend on.

analysis.happening: AirMembrane raised about ¥850M (equity, an SMBC loan and a NEDO grant), led by Global Brain with MUFG Capital; cumulative funding is about ¥1B. Pilot production is planned for 2027 and a mass line in 2028. Its synthesis is claimed over 100x faster than conventional methods.
analysis.now: Japan is strong in chip materials and consumables rather than fabs or GPUs; this is that niche. Caveat: small round, no named customers, no yield or transmission data, and Dealroom reports a different USD figure.
analysis.future: Watch for pellicle qualification with a scanner maker or fab, a larger Series A, and further NEDO grants.

items.headline: PFN and Tenstorrent Win a NEDO Project for Photonics-Linked AI Chiplets, With Up to 60 Months of R&D
items.dek: Japan's AI-chip champion pairs with a US open-architecture CPU firm on a research plan that pays off after FY2031.

analysis.happening: NEDO selected the joint proposal under its post-5G program. PFN builds AI chiplets with 3D-stacked memory; Tenstorrent builds open-architecture CPU chiplets; they link via photonics-electronics integration. R&D runs up to 60 months, with commercialization targeted after FY2031.
analysis.now: Gap: Nvidia ships rack-scale systems today, while Japan's entry is a five-year research plan. Caveats: budget, bandwidth, power figures and the foundry are undisclosed, and selection does not guarantee a product. The item is slightly older than the window.
analysis.future: Watch the reported 2027 slip of PFN's MN-Core L1000, PFN's IPO plans, and whether Rapidus is named as foundry.
